rows.answer: CREDIT stands for GitLab’s six core values: Collaboration, Results for Customers, Efficiency, Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging, Iteration, and Transparency [1].

rows.question: How much money can I get reimbursed per year for growth and development?
rows.answer: You can be reimbursed for up to $10,000 per calendar year for eligible growth and development experiences, provided you meet all eligibility requirements [1]. If an opportunity spans more than one year, costs can be distributed across multiple years, but you still cannot exceed $10,000 expensed per year [3].
rows.judge_reason: It gives the $10,000 per calendar year limit and adds correct eligibility/multi-year details without contradicting the expected answer, though it omits the Navan reimbursement method.

rows.question: How long do I have to exercise my vested stock options after leaving GitLab?
rows.answer: You have a three-month window after your employment ends to exercise your vested stock options, or you lose them [2]. The handbook also describes this as 90 days post-termination to exercise vested options [4]. You can generally exercise options that are vested as of your last day of service [1], while unvested RSUs and options are forfeited on your exit date [4].
rows.judge_reason: It states the 90-day/three-month post-termination exercise window for vested options and that unvested RSUs and options are forfeited on the exit date, matching the expected answer.

rows.question: Can I wipe my own laptop on my last day?
rows.answer: No. You are required to have your laptop wiped on your last day, and you should book an appointment with an IT Ops team member for that day [1]. Under no circumstance should you wipe your own laptop; laptop wipes must be done by an IT Ops team member for logs [1]. You can contact IT via the Compass app in Slack or at it-help@gitlab.com [1].
rows.judge_reason: It states the laptop must be wiped on the last day only by an IT Ops team member for logs and that an appointment should be booked, matching all key facts without contradiction.

rows.question: What is the first thing an onboarding buddy should do?
rows.answer: The first and most important thing an onboarding buddy should do is schedule a call with the new GitLab team member [1]. This can be done in the days before the new team member starts by asking their manager for the new starter’s personal email address, introducing themselves, and asking when a good time would be for an initial coffee chat [1]. They may consider choosing a time toward the end of the new team member’s first day so the new team member has time to digest some of the onboarding issue and can bring questions to the coffee chat [1].
rows.judge_reason: The system states the key fact that the first thing an onboarding buddy should do is schedule a call with the new team member, ideally before they start.

rows.answer: People Operations responds to an employment verification request within 24 hours [1].

rows.question: Is there a cap on how many vacation days I can take?
rows.answer:
The sources don't give a single global answer — whether there's a cap depends on which entity employs you.

- In Canada, GitLab's PTO is explicitly uncapped: "Flexible PTO: No set annual limit - take time off as needed with manager coordination" [4].
- In the Netherlands, the entitlement is framed as a floor rather than a ceiling: a minimum of 20 vacation days annually as per statutory requirements, accruing at 1.67 days/month, with unused days carrying over but expiring July 1st [1]. The same 20-day statutory entitlement running concurrently with GitLab PTO is described in the Netherlands sick/vacation section [6].
- In Belgium, the policy states 20 statutory vacation days annually, front-loaded and not carried over, running concurrently with GitLab PTO [3].
- In Korea, entitlement scales with service: 12 days/year for 0–1 year, 15 days/year for 1–3 years, and one additional day for every two years continuously worked up to a maximum of 25 days/year [5].
- In Brazil, the statutory leave has structuring rules rather than a stated day cap: vacations can be divided into up to 3 periods, one of which must be at least 14 days and the other two at least 5 days each, cannot begin two days before a holiday or weekend, must be taken within the concession period without carryover, and requires at least 30 days' notice (45 recommended) [2]. Once the full statutory leave allowance is exhausted, any ongoing time off is Flex Time Off per GitLab policy [2].

So: no cap is stated for Canada [4], the Netherlands and Belgium figures are minimum statutory entitlements [1][3][6], Korea has a 25-day/year ceiling on accrual [5], and Brazil's constraints are on how leave is scheduled rather than a total [2].
rows.judge_reason: It captures uncapped Flexible PTO for Canada but misses the key >25 consecutive calendar days approval requirement and wrongly suggests there is no single global answer.

rows.question: Will GitLab sponsor my H-1B visa?
rows.answer: No. GitLab does not support any visa that requires sponsorship [2]. The US H-1B is specifically listed among the visas and work permits GitLab does not sponsor [3]. Therefore, GitLab will not sponsor an H-1B visa.
rows.judge_reason: The answer correctly states that GitLab does not sponsor the US H-1B visa and cites that it is listed among visas GitLab does not sponsor.

rows.question: How much does GitLab put into my pension in the UK?
rows.answer: GitLab contributes **4% of your basic salary** to the UK pension scheme [1]. You contribute **5% of your basic salary as a minimum** [1]. For Entitled Workers, GitLab is not required to make a contribution [1].
rows.judge_reason: It states GitLab contributes 4% of basic salary and the employee contributes at least 5%, matching the expected answer, with extra non-contradictory detail.

rows.question: Does GitLab match my 401(k) contributions?
rows.answer: Yes. GitLab matches 50% of your 401(k) contributions on the first 6% of earnings, up to $1,500 annually [1]. The plan also lists immediate eligibility and vesting [1].
rows.judge_reason: The system's answer includes all key facts from the expected answer—50% match on the first 6% of earnings, up to $1,500 annually—with no contradictions.

rows.question: Who needs to approve a $5,000 conference from my growth and development budget?
rows.answer: A $5,000 conference registration would fall in the $1,000.01–$10,000 approval tier, so it requires Manager + VP approval [2]. All G&D applications require manager approval [4], and conference registration fees are eligible for G&D reimbursement [1].
rows.judge_reason: It states that a $5,000 conference requires Manager + VP approval, matching the expected answer.

rows.question: Can I use a 360 review to manage someone's poor performance?
rows.answer: No. The 360 process is meant to support development and provide feedback for individual growth, and 360s should not be used as performance management tools [1]. A 360 should not replace regular, ongoing feedback or serve as a replacement for asking stakeholders and peers how things are going [1]. It represents a single, anonymous point in time and should not be the core data point in performance conversations [1]. The feedback may reinforce performance already observed, but it should not be the only data point used in evaluating performance [2]. If unsatisfactory performance is identified, managers should address it timely and honestly and should not wait for the 360 Feedback process to address performance matters [2]. The 360 feedback may help in talking through examples of strengths or improvement areas, but it is not a performance management tool [1][2].
rows.judge_reason: It states that 360s are for development and should not be used as performance management tools, matching the expected answer with extra consistent detail.

rows.question: How long can I work from another country without changing my official location?
rows.answer: You can work from another country for a maximum of **183 days (approximately 6 months) per calendar year** without completing a long-term relocation request [1][2]. You must still reside in your primary location for at least **183 days per calendar year**, meaning at least half of your time worked must be from your primary location [1][2]. Working in a new location for **more than 183 days** qualifies as a long-term relocation, and your compensation and employment agreement will be updated to reflect the new location [1]. All team members are also required to request approval to relocate before moving [2].
rows.judge_reason: It accurately states the 183-day limit outside the primary location and the requirement to reside there at least 183 days per year.

rows.question: Do engineers in Australia get anything extra for being on call?
rows.answer: Yes—eligible engineers based in Australia in the Development and Infrastructure departments receive time in lieu after on-call shifts [1]. Time in lieu is time off granted for work outside standard working hours [1]. The compensation is ½ day for a 4-hour shift, 1 day for an 8-hour shift, and 3 days for a 24-hour shift [1]. The full shift/state of readiness is compensated, not only the actual time worked [1]. Time in lieu must be taken within 2 weeks of shift completion [1], and it is requested through Workday by selecting “Time Off in Lieu” [1]. This time-in-lieu approach was stated as effective February 1, 2021 for Development and Infrastructure, with other Engineering departments to be reviewed iteratively [1].
rows.judge_reason: It states that Australia-based engineers in Development and Infrastructure receive time in lieu after on-call shifts, matching the expected answer without contradiction.

rows.question: Who should I contact if I experience discrimination at work?
rows.answer: If you believe you have been discriminated against or witnessed discriminatory practices, contact the Chief People Officer, a People Business Partner, or the Team Member Relations Specialist to initiate an investigation [1]. GitLab has also engaged Lighthouse Services to provide anonymous reporting methods [1]. Report suspected discrimination right away and never retaliate against anyone who raises a good faith belief that unlawful discrimination has occurred [1]. For discrimination or retaliation related to military leave, immediately contact Team Member Relations [4].
rows.judge_reason: The system answer includes all three expected contacts—Chief People Officer, People Business Partner, and Team Member Relations Specialist—and adds only consistent extra detail.

rows.question: How long is parental leave in New Zealand, and how much of it is paid?
rows.answer: In New Zealand, a team member who qualifies as a Primary Carer and has been employed for at least six months can receive government-funded parental leave pay, and Primary Carer Leave can last up to 26 weeks [1]. Extended parental leave is unpaid: eligible team members with at least six but less than twelve months’ employment can take up to a total of 26 weeks, less any Primary Carer Leave taken, while those with at least twelve months’ employment can take up to 52 weeks, less Primary Carer Leave with a maximum of 26 weeks deducted [1]. If eligible, GitLab supplements the government-funded payment so the team member receives 100% pay for up to 16 weeks of Parental Leave [2]. For Partner Leave, a spouse or partner of a primary carer with six but less than twelve months’ employment is entitled to one week of unpaid leave, and with at least twelve months’ employment to two weeks of unpaid leave; the sources also state that Partner Leave runs concurrently with GitLab Parental Leave and provides up to 100% of regular salary for up to 16 weeks [2]. Pregnancy-related special leave is up to 10 days of unpaid leave, in addition to primary carer leave [1].
rows.judge_reason: The system states Primary Carer Leave lasts up to 26 weeks with government-funded pay and that GitLab tops up pay to 100% of salary for up to 16 weeks, matching the expected answer.

rows.question: If 100 of my RSUs vest and my tax rate is 30%, how many shares do I keep?
rows.answer: If 100 RSUs vest and your tax rate is 30%, 30 shares are sold to cover the tax, and the remaining shares are placed in your E*TRADE account [1]. So, you would keep **70 shares** [1].
rows.judge_reason: It states 30 shares are sold to cover the tax and that 70 shares are kept, matching the expected answer.

rows.question: Compare what GitLab contributes to retirement savings in the UK and in the US.
rows.answer: In the UK, GitLab provides a Group Personal Pension Plan with Scottish Widows, and GitLab contributes 4% of the employee’s basic salary, while the employee contributes at least 5% of basic salary [2]. In the US, GitLab offers a 401(k) plan with immediate eligibility and vesting, and the company match is 50% of contributions on the first 6% of earnings, up to $1,500 annually [1]. So the UK benefit is described as a fixed 4% employer contribution of basic salary [2], while the US benefit is a matching contribution capped at $1,500 per year [1].
rows.judge_reason: The system accurately states GitLab’s UK 4% basic salary pension contribution and US 401(k) match of 50% of the first 6% of earnings up to $1,500 annually, with extra correct detail.

rows.question: I'm leaving GitLab. What happens to my stock options, and what do I do with my laptop?
rows.answer:
If you leave GitLab, you generally can exercise the stock options that are vested as of your last day of service [3]. You have 90 days after termination to exercise your vested options, and unvested RSUs and options are forfeited on your exit date [4]. If your options have not otherwise expired through termination of employment, they expire 10 years after they were issued [3]. If you leave before you have worked a whole year, the standard one-year cliff means none of your options will be vested [6]. GitLab also directs you to the Stock Options handbook page, specifically the “Exercise Window after Termination” section, for stock option information [1], and says to set up or update accounts you’ll need after your last day, including Carta for stock options [2].

The sources do not say what to do with your laptop. The only related material is under “Your Laptop and Account steps > Other accounts,” which says to set up accounts you’ll need after your last day and ensure your personal email is up to date, including Fidelity, E-Trade, and Carta [2].
rows.judge_reason: It correctly states the 90-day exercise window and forfeiture of unvested options, but it misses the key laptop facts from the expected answer and incorrectly says the sources do not address the laptop.

rows.question: What does MVC mean in GitLab's values?
rows.answer: MVC means **Minimal Valuable Change** [1]. GitLab encourages MVCs to be as small as possible, aiming for the quickest change that improves the user’s outcome [1]. If the change is validated as adding more value than what is already there, it should be done, whether additive or subtractive, without waiting for something more robust [1]. This applies to everything GitLab does across all functions, and for product MVCs there is additional responsibility to validate with customers that useful functionality is being added without obvious bugs or usability issues [1].
rows.judge_reason: It gives the key facts—MVC means Minimal Valuable Change, focused on the smallest and quickest change that improves the user’s outcome—without contradicting them.

rows.question: I got a letter telling me to serve on a jury. What do I need to do?
rows.answer:
Notify your manager as soon as you receive the jury summons and discuss the potential duration and impact on your work responsibilities [1]. Also advise your supervisor of the summons as soon as is practical and provide them with a copy; no Legal Civic Proceeding Leave of Absence will be authorized until a copy of the summons is submitted [3].

Document the absence in Workday by selecting the day(s), clicking “Time-Off,” clicking “Jury Duty,” optionally adding a comment, and clicking “Submit” [1]. Attach a copy of the summons to your Workday entry or email it to leaves@gitlab.com [1]. Create a coverage plan for your responsibilities, set communication expectations during your absence, and plan for your return to work [1]. If a 30-day notice period is not possible, notify your manager as soon as possible and enter the dates in Workday when you can; all team members are required to use Workday as the single source of truth for tracking time off [1].

GitLab provides leave for eligible active team members who receive an official summons or court order to participate in judicial, administrative, or quasi-judicial proceedings, including jury duty, provided they give reasonable notice [6]. Eligible team members receive 100% of weekly wages through paid leave unless the absence exceeds 25 working days; if it exceeds that, Absence Management reviews the case individually [4].

For PTY LTD team members, the handbook separately says team members are entitled to paid community service leave for jury duty, with “make-up pay” for the first 10 days of jury selection and jury duty so they receive 100% of salary for those first 10 days [2]. That leave runs concurrently with GitLab PTO, and PTY LTD team members must select `Military Leave` under the `Leaves` dropdown in Workday and notify their manager as soon as possible with evidence of attendance [2].
rows.judge_reason: It covers telling the supervisor and providing a copy of the summons, entering Jury Duty in Workday, and the requirement that leave is not authorized until the summons copy is submitted.

rows.question: I'm having a baby. How much paid time off do I get as a new parent?
rows.answer:
GitLab provides **16 weeks of paid Parental Leave** for any active team member, regardless of gender, who becomes a parent through childbirth or adoption while working at GitLab [3]. This benefit is available from your first day of employment, provided your child was born or newly adopted during your employment at GitLab [3]. The leave must be used before the child’s first birthday or the first anniversary of the adoption [3]. You may take Parental Leave all at once or split it into up to three segments [3]. If your Parental Leave falls within the 4 scheduled Family and Friends Days, your leave is extended by 4 days [3].

The sources do not give one global total beyond GitLab’s 16 weeks because local statutory entitlements vary. In Denmark, mothers have 4 weeks pregnancy plus 24 weeks maternity leave, with 13 weeks transferable under certain conditions [1]. In Denmark, fathers or co-mothers have 24 weeks paternity leave, with 13 weeks transferable under certain conditions [1]. The maximum Danish maternity and paternity leave payment is **DKK 4,865 per week (2025)** for full-time employees working 37 hours per week [1]. In the Netherlands, statutory partner/paternity leave includes 5 days paid Birth Leave at 100% salary within 4 weeks of birth and 5 weeks paid Additional Birth Leave within 6 months at 70% of maximum day wage [4].

If you need additional time after Parental Leave, you may use GitLab’s Flexible Paid Time Off with manager coordination [6]. You may not extend paid parental leave through Paid Caregiver Sick Time unless you have a family member with a serious health condition [6].
rows.judge_reason: The system gives the key facts—16 weeks paid Parental Leave for any gender from day one, used before the child’s first birthday—and adds non-contradictory detail.

rows.question: Am I expected to work on my birthday?
rows.answer: GitLab encourages team members to take a day of vacation on their special day, in alignment with the Paid Time Off Policy [2]. If the celebration falls over a weekend, team members should take an alternate day such as the Friday before or the Monday after [2]. The sources do not state that you are required or expected to work on your birthday.
rows.judge_reason: It states GitLab encourages taking vacation on your birthday, provides the weekend alternate-day guidance, and notes there is no expectation to work.

rows.question: How far ahead should I tell my boss before taking a week off?
rows.answer: The handbook says to give your manager and relevant team members as much advance notice as possible, and at minimum **at least twice as many days of advance notice as the duration of your planned absence** [1][6]. So for a seven-day week off, that would mean at least **14 days** of advance notice; if you count the week as five business days, the same rule would mean at least **10 business days** [1]. It also lists sharing PTO plans **2–3 weeks in advance or more when possible** as a best practice [3]. You must log the time-away request in Workday [6].
rows.judge_reason: It states the key rule of at least twice as many days of notice as the absence and correctly applies it to a five-business-day week off as at least 10 business days.

rows.question: Do I get extra pay if I fill in for my manager for a few months?
rows.answer:
Potentially, but it is not automatic: GitLab has an **interim bonus** process rather than guaranteed extra pay. For an interim role to be considered, the need for coverage must be longer than 30 days, and the interim role generally has to be at a higher level than the team member’s current role [4]. As a guideline, an interim period should last no less than 30 days and no more than 4 months [1].

If the role is lateral, an interim bonus may be considered only if the team member assumes 100% of the workload of the lateral role for 60 days or more **in addition to their permanent full-time role**, subject to review by the People Business Partner and group leader [4]. For Go-to-Market roles, since 2023-02-01 interim bonuses are available to people managers temporarily occupying a lateral or higher management position in addition to their permanent full-time role [4]. For acting roles, the decision on whether the role meets eligibility criteria rests with the Hiring Manager and Department head [4].

When the interim period ends, the manager should review the Criteria for Eligibility for the Interim Bonus and submit an interim bonus request, including the full bonus calculation in a comment [1]. The manager submits the bonus in Workday as a one-time payment and must provide the interim period’s start and end dates under Additional Information [6]. The team member must still be an active GitLab team member at the end of the interim period to be eligible, and there is no prorated payment if they leave during the interim period [6].
rows.judge_reason: It correctly explains the interim bonus process and eligibility, but it omits the key amount—the greater of the $1,000 standard discretionary bonus or 10% of salary for the interim period.

rows.question: Do I have to answer work emails while I'm on maternity leave?
rows.answer: No. Under GitLab’s Parental Leave policy, you are not required to log into GitLab systems or respond to any work-related emails or deadlines while on leave [1]. You may receive automated system emails during your leave, but you should disregard them because they do not require action from you [1]. Any required approvals will be handled by the team or when you return, and you will not be disadvantaged for being unable to complete approvals during your protected leave [1].
rows.judge_reason: It states that employees are not required to log in or respond to work emails and should disregard automated system emails, matching the expected answer.
